finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::hand-rolled `asciitrim` regex has quadratic (redos-style) worst case on attacker-supplied note content, replacing upstream's linear `string.prototype.trim()`
evidence: Verified at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:19-23 (the regex) and its call site in the setext branch (`asciiTrim(state.getLines(...))`). The alternative `[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$` is unanchored at the start, so a global `replace` retries the greedy run at every offset of an interior whitespace run and backtracks one char per failed `$` check — O(n^2), the same shape as the published trim-newlines ReDoS (CVE-2021-33623), and upstream markdown-it's lheading uses linear `.trim()` instead. The path is reachable (needs a long interior whitespace run in a paragraph followed by a `===`/`---` underline, then re-rendered on every doc change), so a collaborator can persist content that freezes viewers' preview render. I rate it minor rather than higher because it requires deliberately crafted content from an already-authorized workspace member and the blast radius is a hung browser tab, not server/data impact; I could not execute the regex to measure actual timings.
